effects: Moves NFT tokenId of this collection from `from` to `to`. The caller must be the owner, approved for the token, or an operator (ERC721.transferFrom, _isApprovedOrOwner).
Clears any single-token approval on tokenId (_transfer calls _approve(address(0), tokenId)).
formats.shown: Transfer token <collection #id> from <from> to <to>, with From, To and Artwork fields.

effects: Moves NFT tokenId from `from` to `to` (ERC721.safeTransferFrom -> _safeTransfer -> _transfer).
Clears the token's single-token approval.
If `to` is a contract, calls its onERC721Received and reverts unless it accepts the token.
formats.shown: Safely transfer token <collection #id> to <to>, with From, To and Artwork fields.

findings.title: safeTransferFrom: interpolatedIntent leaves out the `from` address that the sibling transferFrom sentence includes.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256) interpolatedIntent "Safely transfer token {tokenId} to {to}". transferFrom uses "Transfer token {tokenId} from {from} to {to}". `from` is a field, so the sentence could carry it. An operator moving someone else's token cannot tell from the sentence whose token it is.

effects: Moves NFT tokenId from `from` to `to` (ERC721.safeTransferFrom -> _safeTransfer).
Clears the token's single-token approval.
If `to` is a contract, calls its onERC721Received with `data` and reverts unless it accepts the token.
formats.shown: Safely transfer token <collection #id> to <to>, with From, To and Artwork fields. The `data` bytes are not shown.

findings.title: safeTransferFrom with data: interpolatedIntent leaves out the `from` address.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256,bytes) interpolatedIntent "Safely transfer token {tokenId} to {to}". `from` is shown only as a separate field.

findings.title: safeTransferFrom with data: the callback `data` bytes are not shown. They move none of the signer's assets.
findings.evidence: ERC721._checkOnERC721Received passes `data` only to IERC721Receiver(to).onERC721Received. descriptor.json has no field for `data`.
findings.fix: None needed. Optionally add a raw `data` field with visible: optional.

effects: Sets `to` as the single approved address for tokenId and replaces any earlier approval (ERC721.approve -> _approve). The caller must be the owner or an operator.
Setting `to` to the zero address clears the token's approval.
formats.shown: Allow <to> to transfer token <collection #id>, with Operator and Artwork fields.

findings.title: approve: approving the zero address revokes the token's approval, but the screen says 'Allow 0x0 to transfer'.
findings.evidence: ERC721._approve sets _tokenApprovals[tokenId] = to, so to = address(0) clears the approval. descriptor.json approve interpolatedIntent "Allow {to} to transfer token {tokenId}" has no special handling for the zero address.
findings.fix: Add a note or a label such as 'Approved address (zero = revoke)'. Wallets that support it can also map the zero address to 'none (revoke)'.

effects: Grants (approved = true) or revokes (approved = false) `operator` the right to transfer, approve and burn every token of this collection the signer owns, now and in the future (ERC721._setApprovalForAll; burnEditions also accepts operators through _isApprovedOrOwner).
formats.shown: "true all tokens for <operator>" with intent 'Set operator approval', and Operator and raw Approved fields.

findings.title: setApprovalForAll: the raw boolean makes the sentence read 'true all tokens for X', so grant or revoke is unclear.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json setApprovalForAll interpolatedIntent "{approved} all tokens for {operator}" with field approved format "raw". Case 4 renders "true all tokens for Test Operator". The intent 'Set operator approval' does not say that it grants control of every token in the collection.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Allow operator to manage all your artworks' and the sentence "Allow {operator} to transfer all your artworks: {approved}". Or map the bool to 'Grant'/'Revoke' and label the field 'Grant full access'.

findings.title: setApprovalForAll: neither intent nor fields say the operator can also burn the signer's artworks.
findings.evidence: FeralfileExhibitionV3.burnEditions requires _isApprovedOrOwner(_msgSender(), id), and that check includes isApprovedForAll(owner, spender). descriptor.json intent "Set operator approval".
findings.fix: Say 'transfer or burn all your artworks' in the intent or the sentence.

effects: Permanently burns each listed edition NFT. The caller must be the owner, approved for the token, or an operator, and the contract must have isBurnable set (FeralfileExhibitionV3.burnEditions -> _burn).
Deletes each edition's IPFS CID registration and edition record.
formats.shown: Permanently destroy selected editions, with each edition listed by name under 'Artworks'.

formats.key: authorizedTransfer((address from,address to,uint256 tokenID,uint256 expireTime,bytes32 r_,bytes32 s_,uint8 v_)[] transferParams_)
effects: Only a trustee or the owner can call it (onlyAuthorized). For each element, it checks the owner's off-chain signature over (from, to, tokenID, expireTime) and the expiry, then safe-transfers tokenID from `from` to `to` (_authorizedTransfer -> _safeTransfer).
Clears each moved token's approval and calls onERC721Received on contract recipients.
formats.shown: Intent 'Authorize artwork transfer', sentence 'Execute authorized artwork transfers', with From, To, Artwork and expiry fields listed per element.

findings.title: authorizedTransfer: the intent says the signer authorizes, but the call executes transfers that owners already signed.
findings.evidence: FeralfileExhibitionV3.authorizedTransfer is onlyAuthorized and _authorizedTransfer moves tokens after isValidRequest checks the owner's signature. descriptor.json intent "Authorize artwork transfer" conflicts with interpolatedIntent "Execute authorized artwork transfers".
findings.fix: Set intent to 'Execute signed artwork transfers'.

findings.title: authorizedTransfer: from, to, tokenID and expiry are shown as separate lists, so a batch's transfers cannot be paired.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json fields use paths transferParams_.[].from, transferParams_.[].to, transferParams_.[].tokenID and transferParams_.[].expireTime as four separate array fields.
findings.fix: Use one field group on path transferParams_.[] with from, to, tokenID and expireTime as nested fields, so each transfer renders together.

formats.key: createArtworks((string title,string artistName,string fingerprint,uint256 editionSize,uint256 AEAmount,uint256 PPAmount)[] artworks_)
effects: Only a trustee or the owner can call it. It registers each artwork with ID keccak256(fingerprint), plus its title, artist, editionSize, AEAmount and PPAmount (_createArtwork).
The number of editions that can later be minted is editionSize + AEAmount + PPAmount (_mintArtwork's range check).
formats.shown: 'Create artworks', with Title, Artist and Edition size listed per artwork.

findings.title: createArtworks: AEAmount and PPAmount are hidden, but they raise the mintable supply above the 'Edition size' shown.
findings.evidence: FeralfileExhibitionV3._mintArtwork requires editionNumber_ < editionSize + AEAmount + PPAmount. descriptor.json createArtworks shows only artworks_.[].title, artistName and editionSize.
findings.fix: Add fields for artworks_.[].AEAmount ('Artist editions') and artworks_.[].PPAmount ('Printer proofs').

findings.title: createArtworks: title, artist and size are shown as separate lists rather than grouped per artwork.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json fields artworks_.[].title, artworks_.[].artistName and artworks_.[].editionSize are separate array fields.
findings.fix: Use a field group on artworks_.[] with nested fields.

formats.key: batchMint((uint256 artworkID,uint256 edition,address artist,address owner,string ipfsCID)[] mintParams_)
effects: Only a trustee or the owner can call it. For each element, it mints edition ID artworkID + edition to the `artist` address (_safeMint, which calls onERC721Received if artist is a contract).
If artist != owner, it then safe-transfers the new token from the artist to `owner`.
Registers the ipfsCID as the token's metadata and emits NewArtworkEdition.
formats.shown: 'Batch mint editions', with Artwork ID (raw), Edition (raw) and Owner listed per mint.

findings.title: batchMint: the `artist` address, which first receives and is recorded as minter of each token, is hidden.
findings.evidence: FeralfileExhibitionV3._mintArtwork: _safeMint(artist_, editionID); if (artist_ != owner_) _safeTransfer(artist_, owner_, editionID, ""). descriptor.json batchMint has no field for mintParams_.[].artist.
findings.fix: Add a field mintParams_.[].artist labeled 'Artist' with format addressName.

findings.title: batchMint: the token minted (artworkID + edition) is not shown; Artwork ID is a raw keccak-sized integer.
findings.evidence: _mintArtwork sets uint256 editionID = artworkID_ + editionNumber_, and artworkID is keccak256(fingerprint) in _createArtwork. descriptor.json shows mintParams_.[].artworkID and .edition as raw, as separate lists.
findings.fix: Group the fields per mint on mintParams_.[]. If the hidden ipfsCID is kept, consider showing it with visible: optional.

effects: Only a trustee or the owner can call it. It sets the address royaltyInfo reports as receiver of secondary-sale royalties for every token (setRoyaltyPayoutAddress; the zero address reverts).
formats.shown: 'Set royalty payout address', with the new address.

effects: Only a trustee or the owner can call it. It replaces the base URI that tokenURI prefixes to every edition's IPFS CID. An empty string falls back to 'ipfs://'.
formats.shown: 'Set token base URI', with the raw string.

findings.title: setTokenBaseURI: an empty base URI means the 'ipfs://' default, which the raw display does not say.
findings.evidence: FeralfileExhibitionV3.tokenURI: if (bytes(baseURI).length == 0) baseURI = "ipfs://". descriptor.json field baseURI_ format raw.
findings.fix: Optionally note in the label 'Base URI (empty = ipfs://)'.

effects: Only a trustee or the owner can call it. It replaces the IPFS CID (the metadata and artwork pointer) of edition tokenId, and frees the old CID's registration.
formats.shown: 'Update edition IPFS CID', with the edition by name and the new CID raw.
